QUESTION:
Which other drugs interact with Prednisone?

RESPONSE:
Short answer: the excerpt you've provided doesn't contain that information. The text supplied covers only the INDICATIONS AND USAGE and DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION sections of the prednisone tablet label — it has no Drug Interactions, Warnings/Precautions, or Contraindications section, so I can't cite label-based interaction statements for you here.

The only drug-combination references in the excerpt are therapeutic rather than cautionary: prednisone is indicated for fulminating or disseminated pulmonary tuberculosis and for tuberculous meningitis with subarachnoid block only when used concurrently with appropriate antituberculous chemotherapy, and in primary/secondary adrenocortical insufficiency it may be used together with mineralocorticoids where applicable.

For general background (not from this excerpt, and not a substitute for the full prescribing information): prednisone labeling typically discusses interactions with CYP3A4 inducers such as rifampin, phenytoin, phenobarbital, and carbamazepine (which can reduce corticosteroid effect); CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ketoconazole, clarithromycin, and ritonavir (which can increase corticosteroid exposure); estrogens/oral contraceptives; NSAIDs and aspirin (increased GI bleeding risk, and corticosteroids can lower salicylate levels); anticoagulants such as warfarin (variable INR effects); potassium-depleting agents such as loop/thiazide diuretics and amphotericin B (hypokalemia); antidiabetic agents (reduced glycemic control); cholinesterase inhibitors in myasthenia gravis; live or live-attenuated vaccines and other immunosuppressants; isoniazid and cyclosporine; and digitalis glycosides (arrhythmia risk with hypokalemia).

Please check the complete FDA prescribing information for your specific prednisone product, or ask your pharmacist or prescriber to review your full medication list, before relying on any of the above.
